items.title: Terri Lyne Carrington interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I know Kenny Barron came this year and Ndugu Chancler, and I don’t think they’re performing they just came.

ctx.x: Welcome. Quite a scene here at the IAJE, isn’t it?

Yeah, it’s always quite a scene, I mean you never know who you’re going to run into, especially depending on what city it’s in. Last year it was in Los Angeles and so I was able to go most of the days because I live in that area, and it was amazing how many people you see at these events, that you don’t run into just maybe once a year at something like this or a lot of times you run into people at the North Sea Jazz Festival in the summer. But IAJE has a way of really bringing people together. I know a lot of…
That’s really great. And people get to meet and greet, especially the people that live on one coast might not see the New York people etcetera.
